Configuring a Modality: AE Title, Port, Modality Worklist, Performed Procedure Step, Storage Commitment

Unit 2: Clinical Engineering. Lesson 11 of 65 in CIIP Academy.

A new ultrasound scanner arrives Monday and the department wants to scan Tuesday. You own the connection to PACS. Do it in a fixed order and test at each step.

The triplet on both ends

Each device has an AE title (up to 16 characters, case-sensitive), an IP address, and a port. The sender needs the receiver's full triplet. The receiver needs the sender's AE title on its allowed list, and often its address as well. The registered DICOM ports are 104 and 11112.

Step by step

  1. Record the new device's AE title, address, and port.
  2. Add it to PACS, the RIS or broker, and any router, and add the PACS triplet to the scanner.
  3. Open the firewall paths needed between them.
  4. Run C-ECHO in both directions.
  5. Test the modality worklist query and check the fields it fills.
  6. Send a test study and check the image count in PACS.
  7. Confirm MPPS and storage commitment.

The worklist

The worklist query returns scheduled procedures so the technician selects the patient instead of typing. It fills patient name, ID, accession number, and requested procedure.

MPPS

MPPS sends an in-progress message when the exam starts and a completed message with the images made. RIS and PACS use these to update status and to spot missing images.

Storage commitment

The modality asks PACS to take responsibility for the stored objects. Only when the commitment arrives may the modality delete its local copy.

What C-ECHO proves

A successful C-ECHO proves titles, address, and port match. It does not prove images will store.

Exam tip: rejected means a wrong AE title, refused means a wrong port or a stopped service, and a timeout points at a firewall. Never let the modality purge before storage commitment.
Remember
Configure AE title, address, and port on both ends, prove it with C-ECHO, then test the worklist, a store, MPPS, and storage commitment before the modality goes live.
Deeper explanation

Configuring a Modality: AE Title, Port, Modality Worklist, Performed Procedure Step, Storage Commitment, explained slowly

A new modality checklist

Use the same checklist for every device. Skipping a step is how scanners go live unable to receive a worklist.

Step   Action                                        Evidence
1      Record AE title, IP address, port             written on the form
2      Add the device to PACS and any router         entry saved, firewall rule open
3      Add the PACS triplet to the device            entry saved
4      Run C-ECHO from the device, then from PACS    both answered
5      Query the modality worklist                   test patient appears with accession
6      Acquire a test exam from the worklist         images sent
7      Check the image count and demographics        match in PACS
8      Confirm the MPPS messages                     in progress and completed seen
9      Confirm storage commitment                    device shows committed, then purges
10     Sign the form                                 name and date

Diagnosing a failed echo

The scanner sends a C-ECHO to PACS and fails. What the failure looks like tells you where to look.

What the device reports          Most likely cause                         First action
Association rejected             PACS does not list the scanner's title    add the exact title, case matched
Connection refused               wrong port or the service is stopped      check the port and the listener
Timeout, no answer               firewall dropping traffic or wrong IP     check the firewall rule and address
Echo works one way only          the reverse entry is missing              add the entry on the other device
Echo works, store fails          SOP class or transfer syntax mismatch     compare the conformance statements

Worked example

A new scanner's echo to PACS is rejected. The installer typed the scanner title as ULTRA1. PACS lists ultra1. AE titles are case-sensitive, so the association is rejected. Correct the entry on PACS to ULTRA1 and repeat the echo. Do not open the firewall further, because the connection itself reached PACS.

Worklist fields

The query fills patient name, patient ID, accession number, and the requested procedure. If the technician still types names, the query is returning nothing or the scanner is not set to use it.

MPPS and commitment

In-progress tells RIS the exam has started. Completed lists the images made, so a missing image can be noticed. Commitment is the last step: only when PACS confirms it has the objects does the scanner purge.
